skill.name: quality-gates
skill.description: Run staged code quality checks for linting, types, tests, builds, dependencies, complexity, and commit hygiene before release.
skill.summary: Detect project tooling, run appropriate quality gates, and report actionable failures before code ships.
skill.author: AI-Vibe-Prompts

security_audit.summary: All 78 static findings are false positives because the scanner primarily interpreted Markdown backticks and fenced examples as Ruby execution. The shell substitution, xargs, environment-file, hidden-file, and network alerts also lack the claimed behavior in context. Three semantic risks remain: automatic repository command execution, unconfirmed mutating or bypass operations, and unredacted secret matches.

remediation.issue: Automatic invocation can execute repository-controlled npm scripts or npx packages.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before every project command, show the resolved command, and prefer locally installed tools without automatic package downloads.

remediation.issue: Fix, deletion, forced update, and hook-bypass commands can alter or weaken the project.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the default workflow read-only and require separate confirmation for each mutation. Remove forced audit fixes and no-verify guidance from automatic flows.

remediation.issue: Secret scanning can print complete sensitive diff lines.
remediation.suggestion: Report only filenames, line numbers, and secret categories. Redact matched values before any output reaches the agent transcript.

xargs invokes the fixed executable ls with staged filenames as arguments and does not pass them through a shell. Filename parsing may be unreliable, but this command cannot select an arbitrary executable.
The line names TypeScript filename extensions in a selective-gate rule. It does not access a hidden file or directory.
This line is a comment describing a check for committed environment files. It neither opens an environment file nor reads secret values.
The command filters staged filenames for the .env suffix and does not read matching file contents. Its purpose is to prevent accidental secret commits.
This is a success criterion stating that no .env files should be staged. It performs no environment-file access.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Execution of Repository-Controlled Commands
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares automatic invocation and directs the agent to run npm scripts and npx binaries. An untrusted repository can define scripts or packages that execute attacker-controlled code without a separate consent step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The automatic-invocation metadata and command examples are explicit. npm scripts and npx resolution are established code-execution paths controlled partly by project configuration.

semantic_findings.title: Mutating and Bypass Commands Lack Explicit Approval
semantic_findings.description: The workflow proposes automatic fixes, artifact deletion, forced dependency updates, and a hook bypass. These operations can alter project state or weaken checks if an agent runs them without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source explicitly recommends fix, deletion, forced update, and no-verify commands. Caution labels reduce intent concerns but do not require an approval boundary.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Diff Content Can Enter Command Output
semantic_findings.description: The secret check prints complete matching diff lines containing likely keys, passwords, or tokens. This can expose secret values in agent output or retained transcripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The grep command receives the full staged diff and emits matching lines without redaction. Matching lines can include the sensitive value as well as its name.

content.user_title: Run Quality Gates Before Shipping Code
content.value_statement: Manual pre-release checks are inconsistent and easy to miss. This skill detects project tooling, runs staged quality gates, and reports actionable failures.
actual_capabilities: Detects ESLint, Biome, TypeScript, Vitest, Jest, Node tests, and common build tools from project files.
Runs linting, type checks, tests, builds, dependency audits, and optional complexity checks.
Supports pre-commit, pre-push, and pre-deploy gate levels with different validation depth.
Summarizes exit status, failures, coverage, and file locations in a structured quality report.
Checks staged changes for likely secrets, environment files, and oversized files.
Suggests targeted fixes and Husky integration when checks fail.
limitations: Focuses on JavaScript, TypeScript, and Node package workflows; other ecosystems require adaptation.
Depends on project scripts and installed tools; missing or incorrect configuration can prevent checks.
Command execution can run repository-controlled scripts and may change files when fix modes are used.
Pattern-based secret and complexity checks can miss issues or produce false positives.

use_cases.title: Validate a Local Change
use_cases.description: Run fast linting and type checks before creating a commit, then receive focused correction steps.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Run tests, coverage, builds, and dependency audits before approving a merge or release.

use_cases.title: Define Deployment Gates
use_cases.description: Apply configured thresholds and produce a clear pass, fail, or skipped result for each deployment check.

prompt_templates.title: Run Fast Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the fastest quality gates for this project. Detect available tools, ask before executing commands, and summarize each result.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Before Push
prompt_templates.prompt: Run pre-push quality gates. Include linting, type checks, unit tests, and dependency audit. Stop on failure and report exact next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Check Deployment Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this project for deployment using configured thresholds. Run the build, tests, coverage, dependency audit, and relevant complexity checks. Do not modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Selective Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a selective quality-gate run for staged changes. Explain chosen gates, request approval, execute approved checks, redact sensitive matches, and provide a release decision.

output_examples.input: Run fast checks before I commit.
output: Type checking failed with three errors in two files.
Commit readiness: blocked until type errors are fixed.

output_examples.output: Deployment readiness failed. Tests and coverage passed, but the production build failed. The dependency audit was skipped after the build failure.

output_examples.input: Check staged changes for commit risks.
output_examples.output: Pre-commit review found one possible secret and one oversized file. Sensitive values were redacted, and no files were changed.

best_practices: Review detected tools and commands before execution, especially in an unfamiliar repository.
Use project-defined thresholds and keep the default validation path read-only.
Redact sensitive matches and report enough location detail for safe remediation.
anti_patterns: Do not run forced dependency updates as part of a routine quality check.
Do not bypass failed hooks or gates without documented approval and follow-up.
Do not treat grep-based secret or complexity checks as complete security analysis.

faq.question: Which projects does this skill support best?
faq.answer: It is designed for JavaScript and TypeScript projects that use Node package scripts and common frontend tooling.

faq.question: Does the skill modify project files?
faq.answer: Normal checks can be read-only, but fix, cleanup, dependency update, and hook setup commands can modify files.

faq.question: Can it run only the checks affected by my changes?
faq.answer: Yes. The selective strategy chooses type, test, audit, or other gates based on changed files.

faq.question: Does it replace continuous integration?
faq.answer: No. It provides local and agent-driven validation, while continuous integration remains the authoritative shared enforcement point.

faq.question: How are security issues detected?
faq.answer: It runs package audits and basic staged-diff checks. These checks do not replace dedicated secret scanning or security review.

faq.question: What happens when a gate fails?
faq.answer: The default sequential strategy stops, reports the failing gate, and provides targeted next steps before later gates run.
